title: Heapless staging and ephemeral kernel switch for low-latency prefill
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Short-context requests (<= 64 tokens) dominate interactive workloads for some customers. Our current prefill pipeline incurs host-side allocations and several small memcpy operations per request that amplify latency and produce threadpool contention during traffic spikes. This ticket implements a two-part approach: 1) replace ephemeral heap allocations in the staging layer with a heapless ring descriptor / pinned-slab mechanism to eliminate allocation stalls and reduce GC-like pressure; 2) add an ephemeral kernel-switch path that routes short-sequence prefill requests to a lightweight, on-device optimized attention kernel with minimal host coordination. Goals: reduce p50/p95 prefill latency for short-context requests, cut host CPU utilization under tail loads, and avoid regressions for longer contexts.
acceptance_criteria: p50 prefill latency (short-context <=64 tokens) reduced by >=15% vs baseline on standard bench
host CPU usage during 99th percentile QPS bursts reduced by >=15% (measured per-core user+system)
no regression >3% in throughput or latency for long-context workloads (>1024 tokens)
automated e2e test that validates zero-copy path correctness across quantized and fp16 kernels
design and ABI changes documented and reviewed; PR merged with +2 infra approvals
proposal_steps: Design: define heapless staging API (descriptor lifecycle, reclamation semantics) and ephemeral-kernel handshake header
Implementation: implement pinned-slab allocator backed by a preallocated pinned memory pool; migrate staging buffers to descriptors that reference the slab
Kernel: add short-sequence kernel variant that accepts descriptor refs and avoids host-synchronous cache flushes; minimize input copy requirements
Scheduler: extend prefill scheduler with a cheap heuristic (seq_len <= 64 && token_count < threshold && request_size < X) to opt into ephemeral kernel path
Threading: refactor host threadpool to use per-core IO pollers for pinned buffer completion to reduce lock contention
Testing: perf harness against short-seq synthetic workload, integration with console perf dashboards and canary rolling
tradeoffs: Complexity: heapless descriptors add lifecycle complexity and a new class of leaks if reclamation is incorrect
Memory: pinned slab increases resident memory footprint slightly (configurable via runtime flags)
Kernel maintenance: the ephemeral kernel is a special-case path that needs parity testing; long-term we prefer consolidating optimizations into the main kernel
Fallbacks: requests that misroute must have deterministic, low-cost fallback to the standard path to avoid failed inference
comments: 2026-02-15 Aisha Patel: Initial write-up and goals. Added acceptance criteria and planned milestones. Linked to design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Heapless+Staging+Design

2026-02-22 Miguel Santos: Prototype of pinned-slab allocator landed on branch feat/heapless-staging. Early microbench shows allocations removed from hot path. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5821
2026-02-28 Elena Gruber (code review): Suggested making slab growth bounded and exposing a per-tenant cap. Also requested metrics for slab utilization and reclamation latency.

2026-03-03 Miguel Santos: Integration test added that verifies descriptor lifecycle across retry / fork scenarios. Observed 9% p50 reduction in single-node synthetic short-seq bench (A100, 64 tokens). Dashboard: https://perf.redwood.ai/dashboards/ENG-889101
2026-03-07 Ops: Noted a small increase (~2%) in resident memory under peak load for the canary; configurable flag heapless_slab_max_mb introduced for rollout control.

2026-03-09 QA: Found a corner-case where pinned-slab returned stale descriptor if request timed out and slab reclamation raced with reuse. Added a gating flag to require explicit reclamation acknowledgement; fixing in next patch.

2026-03-10 Miguel Santos: Rolling canary (10% of traffic) started in us-west-2. Early telemetry: p50 short-seq prefill down 12%, host CPU down 18% during synthetic burst. Still validating correctness under mixed traffic. Next: address reclamation race and add automated e2e zero-copy test.
Blocks: Waiting on kernel ABI update (kernel team ticket KRN-372) to accept descriptor handles directly. Coordination meeting scheduled 2026-03-12.
